title: Snackable Threading — micro-conversation primitives (scratchpad)
content:
Goal: explore a lightweight "snackable thread" primitive — short, resumable micro-conversations optimized for low latency and low token-cost. Personal brainstorming pad: mix of UX ideas, API sketch, experiments to run, and open questions.

Context / motivation:
- Many customers want quick factual Q&A, inline assistant snippets, or mini-guides inside apps. Full sessions are heavy; we can reduce cost and complexity with 'snack' objects: bounded context, cheap resume, immediate answers.
- Aligns with Redwood strengths: prefix caching, KV snapshotting, differential routing.

Core properties (working):
- Lifetime: ephemeral by default (TTL e.g., 2 hours) but can be promoted to persistent (user-saved).
- Token budget: tight token cap per thread (e.g., 512 tokens total) to guarantee unit-cost predictability.
- Resume semantics: ability to resume with a condensed context token (summary or pointer to KV cache).
- Mutability: append-only conversation, with optional patch API (small edits).
- Tooling: quick snapshot/export to main session; can be used as a 'micro-plugin' in larger convo.

User stories (short):
- As an end-user, I want to start a short Q&A and get an answer within 200ms so I can stay in flow.
- As a product engineer, I want an API that creates a snack that costs ~X tokens per minute under typical use.
- As a designer, I want a compact UI component showing snack status (ephemeral/pinned/expired).

API sketch (very rough):
- POST /v1/snacks  { prompt: ..., budget: 500, ttl_seconds: 7200, mode: "ephemeral" } -> returns snack_id, token_estimate, snapshot_key
- GET /v1/snacks/<id>?resume_hint=true  -> returns condensed_context + last_message + metadata
- POST /v1/snacks/<id>/append { content: ..., user_id } -> append and re-score budget
- POST /v1/snacks/<id>/promote { target_session_id } -> export condensed KV into session
- DELETE /v1/snacks/<id> (immediate delete)

Client-side UX notes (ideas):
- Compact chip UI: avatar + one-liner + elapsed time + cost badge. Tap to expand full snack.
- Toast when snack hits budget with 2 actions: "promote" or "compress and continue".
- Quick-save templates: "search", "todo helper", "code snippet explain". Users can start from templates to reduce prompt tokens.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create/append/get snack endpoints implemented and documented in SDKs.
- Snack creation latency <= 250ms (cold path target) for 90th percentile.
- Average token cost per snack < 150 tokens for typical Q&A workload.
- Resume flow restores a <128-token condensed context and allows continuation that feels coherent in user testing.

Experiment matrix (priority):
1) Budget vs coherence: run toy workloads with budgets [128,256,512] and measure answer quality + hallucination rate via micro-eval set. Metric: score on eval (0-1) + token cost.
2) Condense strategies: a) LRU prefix prune; b) auto-summary (LLM) to 64 tokens; c) key-value snapshot and pointer. Measure re-answer accuracy and latency.
3) TTL impact on cache hit: vary TTL [5m,30m,2h] and measure cost/latency for resumed snacks from cached KV.
4) UI experiments: A/B test chip vs anchor UX for clickthrough and perceived speed.

Implementation notes (internals):
- Use existing KV caching layer: store short snapshots keyed by snack_id; enable cheap lookup without loading full model context.
- Quantization-friendly smaller model variant for resuming vs full model for long-form promote. Routing policy: prefer smaller variant for snacks to save cost.
- Batching: group snack inference by small-batch window (20ms) to preserve latency but increase throughput.

Open questions / risks:
- Security: ephemeral snacks might still contain PII — need redaction/hard delete guarantees for promo/delete flows.
- Billing UX: how to surface micro-costs without confusing users? Need per-snack token estimate and monthly view.
- Coherence cliff: what happens when promote moves to full session? Risk of mid-turn semantic drift. Need automatic reconciliation (re-run summary).
- Latency tradeoff: caching helps but adds complexity for cold resume.

To-dos (personal list):
- [ ] Draft minimal API spec and add to SDK stub (JS + Python).
- [ ] Create micro-eval set (20 prompts across search, code, summarization) and run budgets matrix. Ticket: RI-4821 as placeholder.
- [ ] Quick sketch for UI chip and toast (Figma link placeholder).
- [ ] Ask infra about snapshot retention costs — ops sync required.
- [ ] Privacy check: add data retention policy for ephemeral snacks.

Notes / heuristics from prior work:
- Prefix caching reduces cost heavily when small repeated prompts used — prioritize cache key scheme early.
- Users prefer immediate, short answers; don't over-optimize for long context in snack. Keep expectations narrow.

Potential future directions (parking lot):
- Snack sharing: allow user to share a snack link (secure short-lived token) into chat or external.
- Snack templates marketplace: team-shared small automations.
- Server-side triggers: create snack from webhooks (e.g., slack message -> snack).

Quick links / references:
- Related internal notes: /shared_drives/product/snack-ux/initial-deck (need to link).
- Experiment PRs: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1234 (placeholder).

End of scratchpad. This is rough — will iterate. Keep it intentionally loose: mix of UX, API, and infra pointers so we can converge with eng and SRE.

Random brain-dump follow-ups:
- Could we expose snacks as composable objects in the console for power users? Tagging, export to guidance, attach to rollout.
- Consider a "budget auto-scale" mode that increases token budget if user promotes snack to persistent within X timeframe (so they don't lose content).

-- Felicia
